title: Expert Litigator (I) (Col to LtCol) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC
raw_text:
15.     MOS 4453, Expert Litigator (I) (Col to LtCol) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC

    a. Summary. An Expert Litigator is a field grade judge advocate
qualified to serve in the most senior military justice litigation billets.
Expert Litigators have the demonstrated ability to litigate, lead, mentor,
and supervise judge advocates assigned as special trial, trial, defense, and
victims legal counsel (including senior and supervisory litigators) in the
most complex and high-profile cases.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a judge advocate.

            (2) Must be selected by a board established by the SJA to CMC.

        (3) Must possess at least 96 months of cumulative military justice
experience as a special trial counsel, trial counsel, defense counsel,
victims legal counsel, appellate government or defense counsel, military
trial judge, or appellate judge (or corresponding billets within the Office
of Military Commissions); military justice or criminal law instructor at
formal schools; or military justice policy or counsel assistance program
assignments at Headquarters Marine Corps or the Office of the Judge Advocate
General of the Navy. Experience as a state or federal civilian prosecutor or
state or federal public defender or defense counsel, or in a litigation
fellowship, may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

    c. Requirements. Judge Advocate Division, in conjunction with DC, M&RA
(MMOA), is responsible for assignment of this AMOS.

       d.   Duties

            (1) May serve in any other MOS 4402 billet.

        (2) Serve in senior leadership billets requiring skill and experience
in military and criminal law issues at Headquarters Marine Corps.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Lawyers 23-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
